log.say: Cover sheet is doing a lot of work with very little chrome - the drafting-table motif with the REV stamp and NO. GE-01 sells engineering-report vibes before I even tap anything. Play, Levels, How to play - exactly three taps, no clutter.
log.thought: Clean opening. Curious if How to play adds anything the cover art didn't already teach.

note.text: The landing screen teaches the core verb (drag block through same-color gate) with a tiny animated diagram before any tap, and keeps the CTA surface to exactly three buttons. Feels calm and confident, not like a menu screen.

log.say: This is thorough - almost too thorough for a skip-happy hybrid-casual crowd. Shape-plus-color for accessibility up front is great, and I like that it name-drops the colourblind presets and drag-step tuning right here instead of burying them. But it's a full page of reading before Level 1.
log.thought: Nobody skims this on a real first session; theyll bail past the diagram. Worth trusting the diagram more and cutting prose.

note.text: How to play crams Block/Gate/Stone/Moves plus a Reading the board paragraph and a Field report blurb onto one scroll before first play. The top diagram alone teaches the verb; the prose below (colourblind presets, drag step, field report) is reference material a first-timer does not need yet and most will not read.
note.causes: Trying to front-load every settings surface (Inks, Drag step, Field report) into the one screen a player is most likely to skim past.
note.playerImpact: Players who do open this screen either bounce off the wall of text or absorb none of the settings info it is trying to teach them; the diagram already does the real job.
note.positives: The animated corner-turn diagram at the top is the best single teaching moment in the app so far - it shows the one-drag-many-cells rule better than words could.

log.say: That took me six moves against a par of four - I fumbled it by moving the cyan bar before noticing the vertical red piece was sitting directly in its exit column. Once I sidestepped the red block first, the rest fell into a clean one-drag-per-block routine. Nothing on the board told me two different-colored blocks would fight over the same exit lane until I bumped into it.
log.thought: This is a real look-ahead puzzle already at level 4 - a bit early for a mechanic this indirect, but the move budget absorbed my mistake without punishment.

note.text: Level 4 requires noticing that a red vertical block sits inside the cyan block's only possible exit column before the cyan block can leave - solving in the intended par-4 needs planning the red block's move first even though it is not the piece you are focused on. Nothing on the board visually flags that two different-colored blocks share a lane dependency; I had to trial-and-error into the collision (moved cyan first, got a not clear path error, then worked backward).
note.evidence: t018 board, level 4 - moves used 6 vs par 4
note.causes: No visual signal (like a highlight or dependency line) marks that one block's parking spot is inside another's planned exit corridor; the player only discovers it via a failed drag.
note.playerImpact: A generous move-limit cushion (par+4 this early) absorbs the wasted moves so it is not punishing, but it is the first moment the game asks for genuine sequencing foresight rather than pattern-matching a single block to its gate - slightly early for L1-4's stated no-obstacle-pile-on pacing.
note.positives: The error message on a blocked drag (has no clear path out) is specific enough that I could reason backward to the real cause within one extra try.

log.say: This fail card earns its keep. It draws the near miss as a real ghost route on the actual board state, and the copy separates three outcomes in plain language: rescue adds 3 moves AND 3 to my public daily record and swaps my CLEAN token for a plain rescued label, versus Retry or leaving files NOT CLEARED outright. Nothing is fudged and nothing is buried in fine print.
log.thought: Best monetization surface Ive seen this session - wrapping up now, time box is closing.

note.text: The Daily Draft fail card states the three possible outcomes of this moment in full - rescue (+3 moves, +3 on the public record, forfeits the CLEAN token, prints rescued), Retry (fresh attempt), or leaving (files NOT CLEARED) - before the player taps anything, with the ad-gated rescue button clearly AD-tagged. The near-miss block is shown with its real remaining route on the actual board (state truth, not staged). This is the clearest and most honest fail/monetization moment in the build.
